description: Great Lakes Restoration Initiative Pollinator Task Force is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. In order to benefit the pollinators of the Great Lakes Basin, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) funded the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative’s (GLRI) Pollinator Task Force (PTF). Coverage: Great Lakes Basin, Michigan (2021). The toolkit gives Great Lakes Basin, Michigan as the location, 2021 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: In order to benefit the pollinators of the Great Lakes Basin, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) funded the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative’s (GLRI) Pollinator Task Force (PTF). The PTF’s mission is to “catalyze native bee conservation by coordinating and funding actions that efficiently maximize native bee abundance, distribution, diversity and resilience within the Great Lakes Basin.”
